Marin: grabbing handoff now — I'll be primary for the next 8h. quick perms check before I go: PagerDuty escalation access, AWS prod console assume-role, Grafana dashboard edit/view. I'm seeing a 403 on grafana/org when I try to open the inference dashboards :eyes:

IncidentBot: PagerDuty alert INC-2026-421 triggered at 2026-03-14T01:05Z. Current on-call: Samir (primary), Marin (taking over). Active runbook: incident-llm-serving-throttle https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/llm-serving-throttle

Ari: hey Marin — PD: confirm you are in the "inference-primary" escalation policy and have the 'Responder' role. PD web: https://pagerduty.com/orgs/redwood/services. If you don't have it, ping @oncall-admins to add.

Samir: handing off now. current customer impact: degraded throughput in us-west-2 causing higher latencies for hosted-api. no outage yet. token drop rate ~0.8% over last 1m. if it keeps climbing follow runbook step 3 to fail over to the dedicated pool.

Marin: I don't see "inference-primary" in my PD teams, getting "You don't have access to that escalation policy". how do I request quickly?

Ari: fastest route: ask @oncall-admins in Slack — they can add you in ~10-15m. if you need to act immediately, Samir can add you as a responder on the incident (from the PD UI). PD support is slow for urgent adds.

Samir: added Marin as responder on the incident. :thumbsup:

Nora: Grafana note — to view/edit dashboards you need org role 'Editor' for /dashboards/inference. if you see 403 -> run the SSO flow (top-right) then request Editor via the self-service form at https://grafana.redwood.internal/orgs/. if that's blocked, open an infra-ops ticket.

Marin: still getting 403 after SSO, it says "no org role". what CLI/console steps can I use in AWS to avoid being blocked for urgent checks?

Ari: AWS quick: assume the oncall role locally:
```
aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/OncallInProd --role-session-name marin-handoff
export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=...
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...
export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN=...
```
Note: OncallInProd requires MFA. If assume-role fails, ping infra-privs.

Samir: also useful: use SSM to tail logs from the serving nodes:
```
aws ssm start-session --target i-0abcdef12345 --document-name AWS-StartInteractiveCommand --parameters 'commands=["sudo tail -n 200 /var/log/redwood/runtime.log"]'
```
That will avoid needing full console if your role is limited.

IncidentBot: REMINDER: runbook step 2a requires updating the routing policy if token error >= 1% sustained for 5m. See: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/llm-serving-throttle#step-2a

Nora: coverage note — APAC overnight gap 03:00-10:00 UTC isn't fully staffed this week. if anything spikes in ap-east please escalate to the backup list: @apac-backup (Kaito, Mei). we should try to recruit someone for tomorrow — small coverage gap might require a follow-me handoff.

Marin: ack. Samir — can you confirm you granted me Grafana Editor for inference dashboards and that PD responder shows up for me?

Samir: done. I added Editor role in Grafana and confirmed Marin is a PD responder. access should appear within ~30s. let me know if anything still 403s.

Marin: confirmed. got Grafana Editor and PD responder is visible. saving runbook links and starting monitoring. will reroute to dedicated pool if latency trend spikes.

Nora: handoff checklist (paste):
- confirm PD responder + escalation policy
- AWS assume-role + MFA
- Grafana view/edit access to /dashboards/inference
- open autoscaler page and confirm queue length < threshold
- post in #incidents if customer impact >1% for 10m
- record any temporary creds in 1Password (Oncall/Creds)

Samir: small reminder — do NOT paste creds in Slack. always use 1Password shared vault.

Marin: understood. starting 8h primary window. monitoring latency/throughput and will post any mitigation actions here. :eyes:
